gappers.catalyst: Kratos Defense posted a Q2 2026 double beat (revenue + EPS), with business momentum expected to accelerate.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Kratos reported Q2 2026 revenue of $458.8M (+19.1% organic growth), net income up 113.1% to $30.9M, and raised FY organic revenue growth guidance to 19%-23%. Recent operational wins: ~$400M Department of War contract plus counter-drone/space domain awareness awards, a new 167,000 sq ft Pennsylvania manufacturing plant, and a $50M Indiana hypersonic payload facility completed ahead of schedule.
gappers.why: Earnings beat-and-raise (double beat plus a guidance hike) is the textbook mechanism for pulling in momentum buyers; the magnitude of the beat plus concrete contract wins gives the move a fundamental anchor rather than pure headline reaction.
gappers.impact: Premarket volume (251,587 sh) is moderate but not extreme relative to the size of the beat; a raised full-year guide argues this reads as a real repricing, not a one-day spike. Possible sector read-through with other defense/industrials names (AMPX also gapping today on a related aviation/defense-adjacent theme).
gappers.horizon: LONG_TERM - guidance raise and contract backlog are structural, not headline-only, and defense/industrials sit in the early-cycle favored-sector bucket per TRADING-STRATEGY.md's sector rotation table; worth a confluence check on a later /trade pass rather than a same-day fade play.

gappers.catalyst: Coverage today centers on Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway NYT stake hitting all-time highs in 2026 - an unrelated positive framing that predates and does not explain today's decline.
gappers.catalyst_detail: NYT reported Q2 2026 revenue of $762.5M and adjusted EPS of 69 cents, but digital subscriber growth slowed versus prior quarters even as digital subscription revenue grew 16.4% YoY. The company also faces ongoing DOJ subpoenas tied to Air Force One security reporting (DOJ has agreed to withdraw some). The circulating Buffett/Berkshire-stake headline is stale positive coverage, not a fresh catalyst for today's gap down.
gappers.why: Reads as a Q2 earnings reaction - decelerating digital subscriber growth overshadowing a revenue/EPS print that was in line, a classic 'growth deceleration disappoints despite a beat' sell mechanism, not the Buffett headline circulating today.
gappers.impact: Premarket volume (217,446 sh) is moderate. No clear sector-wide read-through identified - media/publishing peer set is thin and no other watchlist name is moving in sympathy, so this looks idiosyncratic to NYT's own subscriber-growth numbers rather than a group move.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM - earnings-reaction gap with no structural catalyst identified beyond a subscriber-growth deceleration; absent confirming details this is a headline/print reaction likely to stabilize within days, not a multi-week thesis.
gappers.opportunity_cost: 0/6 positions open, 0/3 weekly trades used - nothing displaced. Second-ranked by |gap%| but a decliner: fails the Entry Checklist's catalyst leg for a long (the catalyst just fired negative, not positive) and the strategy is long-stocks-only, so this is not an actionable setup today regardless of size.

gappers.catalyst: Jim Cramer issued a bullish call on Amprius Technologies with a $23 price target, calling it 'a good spec' name.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Amprius (silicon-anode lithium-ion batteries for aviation/drone applications) released Q2 2026 earnings today (Aug 5) and raised full-year revenue guidance to at least $130M, building on FY2025 revenue of $73.01M (+202% YoY, still unprofitable with a $44.02M loss). The company has an existing partnership with Matternet for drone-delivery battery applications, and consensus rates it Strong Buy.
gappers.why: Earnings beat plus raised full-year guidance, amplified by a high-profile media buy call (Cramer) same-day, is a beat-and-raise-plus-publicity mechanism that pulls in both fundamental and retail momentum buyers together.
gappers.impact: Premarket volume (451,333 sh) is the largest of today's up-movers, supporting a real repricing rather than headline noise. Possible thematic read-through with KTOS (also gapping today on a defense/aviation-adjacent beat-and-raise) - both serve aviation/defense end markets.
gappers.horizon: LONG_TERM - the guidance raise is structural and the aviation/drone-battery demand story is durable, but the company remains unprofitable, so treat as a candidate for confluence confirmation rather than a same-day chase.
gappers.opportunity_cost: 0/6 positions open, 0/3 weekly trades used - nothing displaced yet, but AMPX and KTOS are both defense/aviation-adjacent gappers today; taking both would need to clear the correlation gate (scripts/corr-gate.mjs, blocks >0.75 correlation with 2+ open positions) and the max-3-new-trades/week cap, so if both later clear confluence this is a rank/size choice, not a guaranteed double-entry.

gappers.catalyst: GlobalFoundries beat Q2 2026 revenue estimates ($1.79B vs $1.76B consensus) but the stock is falling on a Morgan Stanley price-target cut from $65 to $57.
gappers.catalyst_detail: GFS also disclosed a letter of intent for a $300M U.S. government award for silicon photonics R&D, completed its acquisition of Synopsys' Processor IP Solutions Business, and expanded its AI-managed-services collaboration with Infosys. Despite the Q2 beat and these structural positives, Morgan Stanley cut its price target from $65 to $57 today, which appears to be the proximate driver of the premarket decline.
gappers.why: A same-day sell-side downgrade/PT cut overriding an earnings beat and positive strategic news is a 'beat but re-rated down' mechanism - the market is pricing the analyst's forward view over the trailing print.
gappers.impact: Premarket volume (249,874 sh) is moderate. Possible semiconductor-sector read-through worth checking against peer foundry/chip names for confirmation of whether this is GFS-specific downgrade risk or a broader semis re-rating.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM - a single-analyst downgrade against a revenue beat and a government-award positive reads as a near-term overreaction rather than a structural regime change; not enough here to call it a multi-week thesis on today's information alone.
gappers.opportunity_cost: 0/6 positions open, 0/3 weekly trades used - nothing displaced. Fourth-ranked decliner: fails the Entry Checklist's catalyst leg for a long (fresh negative catalyst - the downgrade - dominates today's print) and the strategy is long-stocks-only, so not actionable as scanned even before considering R:R.
